name: Architecture Modelling and Frameworks
summary: Drawing to be understood: diagrams that communicate, decisions on record and the frameworks the corporate market asks for.
prerequisites: Requires patterns and principles — you draw the decision after you know how to make it.
syllabus: UML and the diagrams people actually use
The C4 model: four zoom levels of an architecture
topics: What a diagram is for: communicating, not decorating
UML: use case, class, sequence, component and deployment diagrams
The C4 model: context, containers, components and code
Flow diagrams, state diagrams and context maps
Architecture decision records (ADRs): context, options and consequences
Functional requirements and quality attributes (non-functional requirements)
BABOK: business analysis and structured requirements gathering
TOGAF: the ADM cycle and the layers of enterprise architecture
IAF (Integrated Architecture Framework) and the alternatives
Zachman and an overview of the classic frameworks
Living documentation: where it lives, who maintains it and when it dies
Tools: diagrams as code (Mermaid, PlantUML, Structurizr)
Presenting architecture to technical and non-technical audiences
